title: PLACEHOLDER: Harrowgate Valley Power — outage prediction and field dispatch
source_material:
PLACEHOLDER — fictional, written for the CCR MCP proof of concept. Harrowgate Valley Power is not a real organisation and none of this happened. Replace with a real, approved case study before testers see it.

DELIVERY LEAD'S SUMMARY (project close-out)

Harrowgate Valley Power is a regional electric utility serving about 620,000 customers across a mix of rural and suburban territory. Storm outages were triaged from customer calls, and crews were dispatched by phone from a single operations centre.

We ran a seven-month engagement in three streams:
- An outage prediction model combining weather forecasts, vegetation data and asset age to rank circuits by risk 48 hours ahead of a storm.
- A field-crew mobile app that pushes prioritised work orders and captures restoration status from the field.
- A data platform consolidating SCADA events, smart-meter last-gasp signals and work-order history into one operational view.

MEASURED RESULTS (from Harrowgate's own reporting, first storm season after go-live)
- Average restoration time for storm outages fell from 9.1 hours to 6.4 hours, a 30% reduction. Source: outage management system, storm events compared with the prior season.
- 71% of field crews used the app on every shift by month three.

NOT YET MEASURED
- Harrowgate expects lower overtime cost during storm season. This is an expectation, not a result.

CLIENT INTERVIEW — Priya Raman, VP Grid Operations (notes)
"We used to find out where the damage was from the phones. Now crews are staged before the wind arrives."

NOT FOR PUBLICATION
- The regulator's open inquiry into last year's storm response is confidential.
- Contract value is confidential.
